description: The agent's meta-programming vocabulary — architectural patterns the code-writing cortex consults BEFORE asking for code. Each pattern is a DesignPattern graph node; its applies_when tags + expected_speedup + category drive selection via a substrate query, not a hardcoded Python score. Add patterns by adding entries here; the cortex picks them up automatically on install.
category_inheritance: genlMt → compiler_theory (the soundness vocabulary the agent already knows: denotational / algebraic / extensional / cost / referential_transparency / ub_preservation)

patterns.name: algorithmic_substitution
patterns.definition: Replace the chosen algorithm with one of equal denotation but lower asymptotic or per-step cost. The compiler-theory cost_equivalence category at the algorithm level instead of the instruction level.
patterns.mechanism: Identify the dominant cost in the existing impl; substitute a textbook-equivalent algorithm with lower complexity (Horner for polynomials, Karatsuba for multiplication, Strassen for matmul, FFT for convolution).
patterns.tradeoff: Modern superscalar CPUs may invert the textbook tradeoff for small fixed-size inputs (see polynomial demo's negative Horner result).

patterns.name: lookup_table
patterns.definition: Precompute outputs for every input in a bounded domain; swap the runtime computation for an indexed read.
patterns.mechanism: Build a `static [T; N]` (or const-evaluable equivalent) indexed by input; load instead of compute.
patterns.tradeoff: Binary-size cost proportional to domain size; only wins if domain is small AND lookup is faster than recomputation.

patterns.name: memoization
patterns.definition: Cache results of a pure function keyed by its inputs; subsequent calls with the same inputs return from cache.
patterns.mechanism: Wrap with a `Vec`/`FxHashMap` keyed by input(s); first call computes + stores, later calls fetch.
patterns.tradeoff: Memory grows with distinct call sites; only wins above a hit-rate threshold; cache invalidation needs care.

patterns.name: loop_fusion
patterns.definition: Merge multiple passes over the same data into a single loop — saves per-iteration overhead and improves cache behaviour.
patterns.mechanism: Inline the inner loops of independent passes into one outer loop body.
patterns.tradeoff: Increased register pressure; reduces locality if the fused body grows too large for L1.

patterns.name: simd_vectorization
patterns.definition: Operate on multiple data elements per instruction using the CPU's SIMD lanes.
patterns.mechanism: Use `core::simd` (or platform intrinsics) to process 4/8/16 lanes per iteration; ensure alignment + tail handling.
patterns.tradeoff: Branchy code can't be vectorised; ABI must support SIMD regs; only wins on amenable inner loops.

patterns.name: specialization
patterns.definition: Generate a separate code path for a known shape (small fixed size, known constant operand) — the compiler folds more aggressively when the shape is concrete.
patterns.mechanism: Split into `eval_small` and `eval_general`; dispatch on the calling pattern, let the compiler inline / constfold the specialised path.
patterns.tradeoff: Code-size cost (extra paths); maintenance overhead when general implementation changes.

patterns.name: bit_packing
patterns.definition: Encode small enums or bool tuples into bit positions of a single integer; manipulate via bit ops.
patterns.mechanism: `u8`/`u16`/`u32` holds N independent fields; access via shift + mask.
patterns.tradeoff: Less readable; lots of `& 0x...` and `>> n` arithmetic in the source.

patterns.name: closed_form
patterns.definition: Replace iteration with a mathematical closed-form expression — e.g. sum of n integers as n(n+1)/2, geometric series, etc.
patterns.mechanism: Derive the closed-form analytically; substitute the single expression.
patterns.tradeoff: Requires the analytical identity to exist; numerical stability may differ.
